subject: proving-hall-cases
label: The Proving Hall — floating weapon reliquary cases
notes: RAHEEM'S BRIEF, 2026-08-04: 'not a regular weapon stand, that's not cool. Maybe a weapon altar, a weapon showcase — one weapon of each. A magical staff in a glass case, a magical bow, magical gauntlets, and they're all FLOATING.' The approved tower batch's weapon rack is furniture; this is a monument.

THE WEAPONS ARE CANON, NOT INVENTED. Archetype_Weapon_and_Companion_Reference.md gives ten named weapons per archetype with a stated fantasy role. Using them makes the Proving Hall mean something: it displays the archetypes' signature arms rather than generic loot. Living Staff (Druid — 'continues growing and changing with its wielder'), Judgment Bow (Seraph — 'distant, deliberate punishment'), Open-Hand Gauntlets (Monk — 'protect the hands without replacing martial skill'), Halo Blade (Seraph — 'channels sacred authority').

EVERY WEAPON FLOATS INSIDE ITS CASE, drawn already suspended and clear of the base. That is what makes them animatable — a slow bob or a rotation via POST /objects/{id}/animations at ~2 generations each — and it is why they must not be drawn resting on anything.

PALETTE: the plate's own colours are named explicitly, because that is the layer that actually works for objects. Warm cream sunlit stone and honey-amber wood for the plinths, dark iron and TEAL-GREEN metal for the case frames — the teal fittings are the single strongest tell that an object belongs in this courtyard. The magic glow inside each case is the weapon's own element and is allowed to be loud.

COLOURS SAMPLED FROM THE GAME'S ELEMENT ART (public/assets/elements/): nature green rgb(77,120,70), holy gold rgb(193,144,84), light gold rgb(202,168,76), spirit sky-blue rgb(115,175,206). Each case gets a different one so four cases in a row do not blur together.
NO BAKED GROUND. No floor tile, no paving, no square backing panel. The first fissure arrived with its own slab and it could not blend.
M5.7 is not engaged — no figures. No real-world heraldry.

objects.note: Four reliquary cases, one weapon each, all floating. Different silhouette per case — tall narrow, wide low, short square, tall wide — so a row of them has rhythm instead of repetition.
